questions.prompt: A continuation bet is most attractive when…

choices.text: You have range advantage and the board is dry.
The board is 876 with two suits and you have no pair

questions.explanation: Bet the boards you smash. Check the boards the caller smashes, especially multiway.

questions.prompt: Checking back in position does not mean you give up the hand. It means…

choices.text: You can still bet a later street or win at showdown.

questions.explanation: Position lets you realize equity and choose a later bluff or value bet.

choices.text: Bet tiny on a wet draw-heavy board and huge with air on a dry ace-high board.
Bet larger with a set on a wet board

questions.explanation: Small on dry, larger when you charge draws or value a strong hand. The reverse leaks chips.

questions.prompt: You are in position as the preflop caller, not the raiser, on A72. You should…

choices.text: Not assume the raiser’s c-bet frequency. Your calling range is the one that missed this board.

questions.explanation: The raiser has the range advantage here. Floats and calls need a real hand or a plan, not hope.
